intent.raw_query: Mexico City food and culture, $900 solo, 5 days, any month 2026

experiences.name: Mercado de San Juan Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore one of Mexico City's most beloved gourmet markets, sampling exotic cheeses, fresh ceviche, traditional tacos, and international delicacies. Chat with local vendors and discover ingredients central to Mexican cuisine.

experiences.name: Teotihuacan Pyramids & Street Food
experiences.description: Visit the ancient pre-Aztec pyramids of the Sun and Moon, one of the most iconic archaeological sites in the world. On the way back, stop at a roadside tlayuda or barbacoa stall for an authentic local meal.
experiences.location: Teotihuacan, State of Mexico (day trip from CDMX)

experiences.name: Coyoacán Neighborhood Walk & Frida Kahlo Museum
experiences.description: Stroll through the bohemian cobblestone streets of Coyoacán, visit the iconic Casa Azul (Frida Kahlo Museum), browse artisan markets, and enjoy a traditional Mexican hot chocolate with churros at a local café.

experiences.name: Tacos al Pastor Crawl in Roma & Condesa
experiences.description: Embark on a self-guided taco crawl through the trendy Roma and Condesa neighborhoods, tasting tacos al pastor, suadero, and carnitas from legendary taquerías like El Huequito and Los Cocuyos. Pair with fresh agua fresca.

experiences.name: Palacio de Bellas Artes & Muralist Art Tour
experiences.description: Visit the stunning Art Nouveau Palacio de Bellas Artes to admire world-famous murals by Diego Rivera, José Clemente Orozco, and David Alfaro Siqueiros. Explore the surrounding Alameda Central park and nearby murals for a deep dive into Mexican cultural identity.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Mexico City
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight UA arrives at 22:30. Rest and settle into Aegean Bliss Resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: No afternoon activities — arrival is late evening. Prepare for the trip ahead.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Mexico City airport at 22:30. Take the Metro Line 5 from Terminal Aérea station (very budget-friendly at ~$0.25 USD) or a pre-booked authorized airport taxi to the hotel. Check in, freshen up, and take a short walk around the immediate neighborhood to get oriented.

meals.dinner: Grab a late-night taco from a street taco stand near the hotel (tacos al pastor or de canasta, ~$0.50–$1 USD each). Many street vendors operate past midnight in Mexico City.

day_by_day.notes: Keep pesos handy for the Metro and street food. Authorized airport taxis cost ~$15–$25 USD and are safer than hailing a cab outside. Download the CDMX Metro app for navigation. Exchange some currency at the airport or use a no-fee ATM.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day at the iconic Zócalo (Plaza de la Constitución), one of the largest public squares in the world. Explore the Metropolitan Cathedral (free entry) and admire the exterior of the National Palace. Walk through the surrounding historic streets of Centro Histórico.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Templo Mayor archaeological site and museum (~$4 USD entry). This ancient Aztec temple is one of the most significant historical sites in Mexico City. Afterward, stroll through the nearby Mercado de Artesanías for local crafts and souvenirs at bargain prices.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the lively streets of Centro Histórico at dusk when the buildings are beautifully lit. Head to Calle Regina, a pedestrian street filled with affordable restaurants, street performers, and a vibrant local atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Eat at a local mercado breakfast spot near the hotel — try chilaquiles or tamales with atole (~$2–$4 USD). Look for 'desayunos' signs.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Mercado de San Juan or a nearby fondas (small family-run eateries) inside a market — a full comida corrida (set lunch with soup, main, and drink) costs ~$3–$5 USD.
meals.dinner: Street tacos and quesadillas on Calle Regina or nearby — budget ~$3–$6 USD for a filling meal with agua fresca.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — Centro Histórico is best explored on foot. Keep bags secure in crowded areas. Most museums are free on Sundays for Mexican citizens but still affordable for tourists on weekdays.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Metro to Coyoacán (Line 3 to Viveros station, ~$0.25 USD). Explore this charming bohemian neighborhood on foot. Visit the colorful Jardín Centenario and Plaza Hidalgo, the heart of Coyoacán. Browse the weekend artisan market stalls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Frida Kahlo Museum (Casa Azul) — book tickets online in advance (~$10 USD, one of the most visited museums in Mexico). Afterward, walk to the nearby León Trotsky Museum (~$3 USD) for a fascinating historical perspective. Explore the cobblestone streets and murals of the neighborhood.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the city center via Metro. Head to the Roma or Condesa neighborhood for an evening stroll through tree-lined streets, art deco architecture, and lively parks. These trendy neighborhoods offer great budget eats alongside upscale options.

meals.breakfast: Try tostadas de tinga or enfrijoladas at Mercado de Coyoacán — a local favorite for breakfast (~$2–$4 USD).
meals.lunch: Eat at Mercado de Coyoacán food stalls — try tostadas, pozole, or fresh ceviche (~$3–$5 USD). This market is famous for its affordable and delicious food.
meals.dinner: Grab tacos or tortas at a local taquería in Roma Norte — look for busy spots with lines of locals, a sure sign of quality and value (~$4–$7 USD).

day_by_day.notes: Frida Kahlo Museum tickets sell out fast — book at least a few days in advance online at museofridakahlo.org.mx. Coyoacán is very walkable and safe for tourists. The Metro is the most budget-friendly way to get around the city.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Teotihuacán, the ancient pre-Aztec city with massive pyramids (~35 miles from the city). Catch an early bus from Terminal Central del Norte (Metro Line 5 to Autobuses del Norte, then a direct bus for ~$3 USD round trip). Arrive early to beat the crowds and heat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Climb the Pyramid of the Sun and Pyramid of the Moon, walk the Avenue of the Dead, and explore the Palace of Quetzalpapalotl. The site entry is ~$5 USD. Spend 3–4 hours exploring this UNESCO World Heritage Site at your own pace.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Mexico City by late afternoon. Head to Garibaldi Plaza in the evening to experience the famous Mariachi Square — free to enter and watch performances, though tipping musicians is appreciated. Soak in the festive atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast before departure — grab pan dulce (sweet bread) and café de olla from a street vendor or bakery near the Metro (~$1–$2 USD).
meals.lunch: Eat at one of the food stalls just outside the Teotihuacán archaeological zone — try barbacoa tacos, tlayudas, or grilled corn (elote) (~$3–$5 USD). Bring water as it can be hot.
meals.dinner: Dinner near Garibaldi — try pozole or birria at a local restaurant in the area (~$4–$7 USD). Many affordable traditional restaurants surround the plaza.

day_by_day.notes: Start early for Teotihuacán — aim to be at the site by 9:00 AM to avoid midday heat and crowds. Wear sunscreen, a hat, and bring water. Buses from Terminal del Norte run frequently (every 30 min) and are clearly marked 'Teotihuacán.' Avoid overpaying for souvenirs at the site — bargain confidently.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Chapultepec Park, one of the largest urban parks in the world (free entry). Explore the park's lakes, monuments, and gardens. Visit the Castillo de Chapultepec (National History Museum, ~$3 USD) for panoramic views of the city and fascinating exhibits on Mexican history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the adjacent Museo Nacional de Antropología (National Museum of Anthropology, ~$4 USD) — one of the best museums in Latin America, housing the famous Aztec Sun Stone and extensive pre-Columbian collections. Spend 2–3 hours here. Afterward, browse the Paseo de la Reforma boulevard.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Mexico City — return to a favorite neighborhood for last-minute souvenir shopping and a farewell dinner. Consider revisiting a beloved taco spot or trying something new like mole enchiladas or chiles en nogada at a local restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a café in Condesa or Roma — try huevos rancheros or molletes at a local comedor (~$3–$5 USD).
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch in Chapultepec Park — pick up fresh fruit, elotes (grilled corn), and snacks from park vendors (~$2–$4 USD) or eat at the park's affordable food stalls.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a traditional Mexican restaurant — splurge slightly on a sit-down meal with mole, enchiladas, and a horchata or Jamaica agua fresca (~$6–$10 USD). Mercado de Medellín in Roma is a great local option.

day_by_day.notes: The National Museum of Anthropology is free on Sundays for all visitors — if Day 5 falls on a Sunday, take advantage of this. Chapultepec Park is best on weekdays to avoid weekend crowds. Keep receipts and pack carefully in the evening if departing the next day. Mexico City's tap water is not safe to drink — stick to bottled or filtered water throughout the trip.

trip_options.title: Classic Mexico City Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — late night arrival. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort and rest.
day_by_day.afternoon: No afternoon activities — arrival is at 22:30. Settle into your room and freshen up.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Mexico City airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take an authorized airport taxi or pre-booked transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in and get a good night's rest to prepare for the days ahead.

meals.dinner: Grab a light late-night snack at the hotel bar or a nearby 24-hour taqueria such as El Farolito if you arrive hungry. Budget around $5–$10 USD.

day_by_day.notes: Flight arrives late at night. Do not schedule any sightseeing on Day 1. Confirm your hotel transfer in advance. Keep some Mexican pesos handy for tips and small purchases upon arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Start your first full day with a leisurely hotel breakfast, then head to the historic Centro Histórico. Visit the iconic Zócalo (Plaza de la Constitución), one of the largest public squares in the world. Explore the stunning Metropolitan Cathedral and walk around the exterior of the Templo Mayor archaeological site.
day_by_day.afternoon: Enter the Templo Mayor Museum (approx. $5 USD entry) to explore ancient Aztec ruins and artifacts. Afterward, stroll through the nearby Palacio de Bellas Artes to admire its stunning Art Nouveau and Art Deco architecture. Browse the artisan market at Mercado de Artesanías La Ciudadela for local crafts and souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Take a leisurely evening walk through the illuminated Centro Histórico. Enjoy the vibrant street atmosphere around Avenida Madero, a pedestrian-friendly street lined with historic buildings, street performers, and vendors.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort or a nearby café. Budget $8–$12 USD.
meals.lunch: Try Café de Tacuba, a historic restaurant in Centro Histórico serving traditional Mexican dishes like enchiladas and tamales. Budget $12–$18 USD.
meals.dinner: Dine at El Cardenal, a beloved mid-range restaurant known for authentic Mexican cuisine including chiles en nogada and traditional soups. Budget $18–$25 USD.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — Centro Histórico involves a lot of walking on cobblestones. The area is very safe during the day and early evening but stay aware of your surroundings. Metro Line 2 (Zócalo station) is a cheap and easy way to get there from most areas.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the world-renowned Museo Nacional de Antropología (National Museum of Anthropology) in Chapultepec Park. This is a must-see for culture lovers, housing the famous Aztec Sun Stone and vast collections of pre-Columbian artifacts. Plan at least 2–3 hours here. Entry is approximately $4–$5 USD.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the museum, explore Bosque de Chapultepec, one of the largest urban parks in the Western Hemisphere. Walk through the park, visit Chapultepec Castle (Castillo de Chapultepec) for panoramic views of the city and exhibits on Mexican history. Entry to the castle is approximately $3–$4 USD.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the trendy Polanco neighborhood adjacent to Chapultepec. Browse upscale boutiques along Presidente Masaryk Avenue and soak in the cosmopolitan atmosphere. This is an ideal area for a relaxed evening stroll.

meals.breakfast: Stop at a local panadería (bakery) or café near the hotel for fresh pan dulce and coffee. Budget $4–$7 USD.
meals.lunch: Enjoy lunch at a casual restaurant or food stall inside or near Chapultepec Park. Try tacos de canasta or tortas from a local vendor. Budget $6–$10 USD.
meals.dinner: Dine in Polanco at Pujol's more accessible neighbor, Lalo!, or try Quintonil's bar menu for modern Mexican cuisine at mid-range prices. Alternatively, visit Contramar for fresh seafood in a lively setting. Budget $20–$30 USD.

day_by_day.notes: Chapultepec Park and the Anthropology Museum are closed on Mondays. Plan accordingly. The park can be crowded on weekends — arrive early for the best experience. Uber is reliable and affordable in Mexico City for getting between neighborhoods.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning trip to the colorful neighborhood of Coyoacán, about 30–40 minutes from the city center by Uber or Metro. Visit the Frida Kahlo Museum (Casa Azul / Blue House) — book tickets in advance online as they sell out quickly. Entry is approximately $10–$12 USD. Explore the vibrant cobblestone streets and colonial architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: After Coyoacán, head to the nearby neighborhood of Xochimilco for a traditional trajinera (colorful flat-bottomed boat) ride through the ancient canals — a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Hire a boat for 1–2 hours and enjoy the festive atmosphere with local mariachi musicians and food vendors on the water. Cost is approximately $15–$25 USD per boat per hour.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the city center and explore the Roma Norte neighborhood, known for its Art Nouveau architecture, independent bookstores, galleries, and vibrant café culture. Walk along Álvaro Obregón Avenue and enjoy the laid-back, bohemian atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or grab fresh fruit and a torta from a street vendor near Coyoacán market. Budget $4–$8 USD.
meals.lunch: Eat at Mercado de Coyoacán — try the famous tostadas de tinga or enfrijoladas from the market stalls. An authentic, affordable local experience. Budget $6–$10 USD.
meals.dinner: Have dinner in Roma Norte at Maximo Bistrot or Fonda Fina, both known for creative takes on Mexican classics in a relaxed, mid-range setting. Budget $18–$28 USD.

day_by_day.notes: Book Frida Kahlo Museum tickets at least 2–3 weeks in advance at museofridakahlo.org.mx — walk-in tickets are rarely available. Xochimilco is best visited on weekdays to avoid large crowds. Bring sunscreen and a hat as the canal ride is mostly in the open sun.

day_by_day.morning: Take a half-day trip to the ancient pyramids of Teotihuacán, located about 50 km northeast of Mexico City (roughly 1 hour by car or organized tour). Climb the Pyramid of the Sun and the Pyramid of the Moon, and walk the Avenue of the Dead. This is one of the most impressive archaeological sites in the Americas. Entry is approximately $5 USD. Depart early (8:00–8:30 AM) to beat the crowds and heat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Mexico City by early afternoon. Visit the Mercado de la Merced or Mercado Jamaica for a vibrant, authentic local market experience — perfect for picking up spices, local snacks, and last-minute souvenirs. Alternatively, spend a relaxed afternoon at the hotel or exploring the neighborhood around your accommodation.
day_by_day.evening: Spend your final evening in the lively Condesa neighborhood. Enjoy a farewell dinner and take a nighttime stroll through Parque México, surrounded by Art Deco buildings and lush greenery. Reflect on your Mexico City experience.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before departing for Teotihuacán. Budget $8–$12 USD.
meals.lunch: Have lunch near the Teotihuacán site at La Gruta, a unique restaurant set inside a natural cave/grotto near the pyramids. A memorable mid-range dining experience. Budget $15–$22 USD.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner in Condesa at El Pescadito for fresh tacos de pescado (fish tacos) or Nevería Roxy for a casual, beloved local experience. For a slightly more upscale option, try Amaya for modern Mexican cuisine. Budget $15–$25 USD.

day_by_day.notes: For Teotihuacán, take an organized tour from your hotel or book a direct shuttle from Central de Autobuses del Norte (Norte Bus Terminal) — buses depart frequently and cost around $3–$5 USD each way. Wear very comfortable shoes and bring water as the pyramid site is large and exposed. Start early to avoid midday heat and tour groups.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Mexico City Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — late night arrival. Rest and settle into the Aegean Bliss Resort after landing at 22:30.
day_by_day.evening: Upon arrival, enjoy a welcome nightcap at the hotel's rooftop bar or lounge. Request a late-night in-room dining experience featuring light Mexican fare such as guacamole, quesadillas, and a selection of premium mezcals to begin acclimating to local flavors.

meals.dinner: Late-night in-room dining at Aegean Bliss Resort — curated Mexican comfort bites and premium mezcal tasting

day_by_day.notes: Flight UA arrives at 22:30. Allow 60–90 minutes for immigration, baggage claim, and private transfer to the hotel. Pre-arrange a luxury airport transfer (black car or private SUV) through the concierge. No activities scheduled before arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely breakfast at the hotel, then embark on a private guided tour of the Historic Centro. Visit the magnificent Zócalo (Plaza de la Constitución), explore the stunning Metropolitan Cathedral, and walk through the ancient Aztec ruins of Templo Mayor with a dedicated archaeologist guide who provides exclusive insight into pre-Hispanic civilization.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Palacio de Bellas Artes for a curated private art tour of its iconic murals by Diego Rivera and other Mexican masters. Afterward, stroll through the Alameda Central park and visit the Museo Franz Mayer for an immersive look at colonial decorative arts. Arrange a private docent for a truly personalized cultural experience.
day_by_day.evening: Dine at Pujol, one of Latin America's most celebrated restaurants helmed by Chef Enrique Olvera. Experience the legendary Mole Madre tasting menu paired with an expertly curated wine and mezcal selection. Reserve well in advance through the hotel concierge.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast buffet or à la carte at Aegean Bliss Resort's signature restaurant — fresh tropical fruits, chilaquiles, and artisan coffee
meals.lunch: El Cardenal — a historic and beloved fine-dining institution in Centro Histórico renowned for traditional Mexican cuisine; try the mole negro and freshly made tortillas
meals.dinner: Pujol — world-renowned tasting menu featuring modern Mexican haute cuisine; budget approximately $150–$200 USD per person

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes for the Centro tour. Book Pujol reservations at least 4–6 weeks in advance. Private guided tours can be arranged through the hotel concierge for a premium, crowd-free experience.

day_by_day.morning: Private transfer to Xochimilco for an exclusive trajinera (flower boat) experience on the ancient canals — a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Arrange a luxury private boat decorated with flowers, accompanied by a personal guide, live marimba musicians, and a floating breakfast spread of traditional Mexican delicacies.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the nearby Frida Kahlo Museum (La Casa Azul) in Coyoacán with a private guided tour that bypasses public queues. Explore the cobblestone streets of Coyoacán, one of Mexico City's most charming neighborhoods. Browse artisan markets and visit the León Trotsky Museum for a deeper dive into Mexico's fascinating political history.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Polanco district — Mexico City's most upscale neighborhood. Enjoy cocktails at a chic rooftop bar such as Terraza Cha Cha Chá, then dine at Quintonil, another globally acclaimed restaurant by Chef Jorge Vallejo, known for its innovative take on Mexican ingredients and biodiversity.

meals.breakfast: Floating breakfast on the trajinera in Xochimilco — fresh fruit, tamales, pan dulce, café de olla, and fresh-squeezed juices
meals.lunch: La Bipolar or Merendero Las Lupitas in Coyoacán — authentic local eateries with exceptional traditional Mexican dishes in a charming neighborhood setting
meals.dinner: Quintonil — chef's tasting menu celebrating Mexican biodiversity and seasonal ingredients; budget approximately $120–$180 USD per person

day_by_day.notes: Book Frida Kahlo Museum tickets well in advance as they sell out quickly. The private trajinera experience should be arranged through a luxury tour operator or the hotel concierge to ensure exclusivity and quality. Coyoacán is best explored on foot.

day_by_day.morning: Early private transfer to Teotihuacán, the ancient Mesoamerican city of pyramids, approximately 50 km from Mexico City. Enjoy an exclusive sunrise tour of the Pyramid of the Sun and Pyramid of the Moon with a private archaeologist guide — arriving before the public crowds for a truly magical experience. Optional hot air balloon ride over the pyramids at dawn for breathtaking aerial views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Mexico City and spend the afternoon exploring the upscale Polanco and Lomas de Chapultepec neighborhoods. Visit the world-class Museo Nacional de Antropología (National Museum of Anthropology) in Chapultepec Park — one of the greatest archaeology museums in the world — with a private guided tour. Stroll through the vast Bosque de Chapultepec (Chapultepec Forest).
day_by_day.evening: Indulge in a premium mezcal and tequila tasting experience at a curated mezcalería such as La Botica or Bósforo, guided by a certified spirits sommelier. Follow with dinner at Dulce Patria, Chef Martha Ortiz's vibrant restaurant celebrating Mexican femininity, culture, and cuisine with theatrical flair.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast box prepared by the hotel — artisan pastries, fruit, and thermos coffee for the Teotihuacán sunrise tour
meals.lunch: La Gruta — a remarkable restaurant set inside a natural cave near Teotihuacán, serving traditional Mexican cuisine in an extraordinary underground setting
meals.dinner: Dulce Patria in Polanco — innovative Mexican cuisine with artistic presentation; budget approximately $100–$150 USD per person

day_by_day.notes: The hot air balloon over Teotihuacán (operated by Globos Aeroestación) should be booked in advance and is weather-dependent. Depart by 5:00–5:30 AM for the sunrise experience. Wear layered clothing as early morning temperatures at the pyramids can be cool.

day_by_day.morning: Begin the final morning with a private Mexican cooking class led by a celebrated local chef. Learn to prepare traditional dishes such as mole, tamales, and salsas using fresh market ingredients. Start with a guided tour of a local mercado (such as Mercado de Medellín) to source ingredients and experience authentic neighborhood life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Museo Soumaya in Polanco — a stunning privately owned museum housing one of Latin America's largest art collections, including works by Rodin, Dalí, and Picasso. Explore the adjacent Museo Jumex for cutting-edge contemporary art. Spend remaining afternoon hours shopping along Presidente Masaryk Avenue — Mexico City's equivalent of the Champs-Élysées — featuring luxury boutiques and designer stores.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at Contramar, an iconic Mexico City seafood institution beloved by locals and food critics alike. Savor the legendary tuna tostadas and signature red-and-green grilled fish. End the evening with after-dinner drinks and live jazz at a sophisticated bar such as Maison Artemisia or Patrick Miller for a memorable final night in the city.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the cooking class's market tour — fresh-squeezed juices, tamales, and local street food tastings at Mercado de Medellín
meals.lunch: Dishes prepared during the private cooking class — enjoy the fruits of your culinary labor with wine pairings
meals.dinner: Contramar — legendary Mexico City seafood restaurant; iconic, vibrant, and beloved; budget approximately $80–$120 USD per person

day_by_day.notes: Confirm departure details with the hotel concierge and arrange a private luxury transfer to the airport if departing the following day. The cooking class should be booked through a premium culinary experience provider such as Eat Mexico or a hotel-recommended chef. Museo Soumaya is free to enter — a rare luxury in itself.
